newsitem.title: USA: SARA LEE HITS FINANCIAL TARGETS FOR FY97.
newsitem.headline: SARA LEE HITS FINANCIAL TARGETS FOR FY97.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp, the food and consumer products company, said it had record cash flow from operations in fiscal 1997 of more than $1.4 billion.
"We are very confident (cash from from operations) was above our record level of $1.4 billion set in fiscal 1995," Janet Bergman, vice president of investor relations, said.
The exact amount of cash flow from operations for fiscal 1997 ended June 30 was not available.
In fiscal 1996, cash flow from operations was $1.3 billion.

Sara Lee's return on equity (ROE) in fiscal 1997 was close to 22 percent and above its 21.5 percent ROE in fiscal 1996, Bergman said. Return on invested capital (ROIC) was "slightly above" the 15 percent ROIC in fiscal 1996.
"In ROE, the goal is over 20 percent. For ROIC, the goal is over 15 percent," Bergman explained.
She added that Sara Lee's growth in inflation-adjusted or "real" earnings per share was over eight percent in fiscal 1997, meeting another financial target.
Additionally, the ratio of total debt to total capital was in the "mid-30's percent," meeting Sara Lee's target of a ratio less than 40 percent, Bergman said.
Earlier, Sara Lee reported earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.57 a primary share, up from $0.52 a year ago. Bergman said earnings were in line with expectations.
She acknowledged there are some concerns that a strong U.S. dollar may hamper growth in Sara Lee's operating income in the near-term.

As previously reported, Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said operating income was up by only a single digit percentage for the fourth quarter and fiscal 1997, largely due to the effect of foreign currencies. Ghez downgraded Sara Lee today to market performer from market outperform.
Bergman said Sara Lee hedges its exposure to foreign currencies to limit the impact on earnings per share.
Sara Lee shares were off 1-4/16 at 43-7/16.
